text:
mike: heads up — noticed a burst of quick reconnects from a beta tenant; console shows ~2x token counts for what looks like the same logical session. anyone seen this?
lia: yup saw that too. sampling logs show 429 then immediate ws reopen within 300-700ms. :thinking:
sam: wait — do we currently count resumes as brand new sessions for billing? that would explain the doubling
tara: billing pipeline aggregates by conn_id. resume uses a different resume_id so we end up double-counting when conn_id changes
mike: snippet from logs: 
```
WARN reconnect: tenant=beta123 code=429 retry_ms=350 resume_id=abc123 conn_id=uuid-987
```
lia: propose adding resume_id as a first-class telemetry tag so console can dedupe and we can show resume-aware metrics
sam: short-term we could also add a server-side debounce that coalesces reconnects within a small window (eg 2s) and attribute to prior session
tara: be careful — coalescing can increase perceived failover latency for some mobile clients. needs to be configurable per route/tier
ops-bot: ops-bot: INC-4321 created and assigned to eng-platform-oncall
mike: UX note: dashboard groups by conn_id today. we should add a "resume-aware" view that dedups on resume_id and shows estimated token-savings
lia: telemetry schema suggestion: add field session_lifecycle with values [created, resumed, terminated] and a reconnect_reason enum
sam: quick hotfix idea: if resume_id present and previous_session.last_seen < 5s, attribute tokens to previous session for billing and mark metric as resumed
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rolled out eng-platform v1.42.3 to us-west at 2024-06-12T10:03Z
tara: plan = hotfix (5s attribution) + dashboard toggle + longer-term: route-level policy for debounce and resume semantics. ok?
mike: SGTM. I'll open the PR for the billing hotfix and a dashboard mock. assigning to @sam and @lia :thumbsup:
